options.text: wartime factory jobs in northern cities
the passage of the Nineteenth Amendment
options.misconception: The Nineteenth Amendment gave women the vote; it did not move workers to northern factories.

options.text: the closing of Ellis Island to immigrants

options.text: the end of segregation in southern states
options.misconception: Background from the books: segregation stayed in place in the South; escaping it was a reason to leave.

rationales.A: Northern factories needed workers for war production, and the draft and the fall in European immigration left those jobs open to Black migrants from the South.
rationales.B: The Nineteenth Amendment gave women the vote. It did not move workers to northern factories.
rationales.C: Background from the books: European immigration fell during the war, but Ellis Island did not close.
rationales.D: Background from the books: segregation stayed in place in the South; escaping it was a reason to leave.
rationales.general:
1. Name the change: hundreds of thousands of Black southerners moved to northern cities.
2. Ask what pulled them. Northern factories were hiring for war work and could not fill the jobs.
3. Ask what pushed them. Jim Crow and violence in the South made leaving attractive.
Remember: migration usually has a pull and a push, so check both before you choose.
